import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_66/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_66/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# According to operation history:
# 1) Join Source2_66_0 and Source2_66_1 on 'school_name' (already done in intermediate_step1)
# 2) Group by Source2_66_1.school_name and aggregate avg(reading_score) (already done in intermediate_step2)

# We will replicate the second operation directly on Source2_66_1 (df1),
# because the join with df0 is not necessary for the final target columns,
# and the target examples show only school_name and reading_score (average).

# Group by school_name and calculate average reading_score as float
target_df = df1.groupby('school_name', as_index=False)['reading_score'].mean()

# Ensure reading_score is float type (it should be by default)
target_df['reading_score'] = target_df['reading_score'].astype(float)

# Sort by reading_score descending to match the example order (optional)
target_df = target_df.sort_values(by='reading_score', ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)

# Write the result to the specified path without the index
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_66/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_66/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_66/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on school_name (inner join to keep only matching schools)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="school_name", how="inner")

# Group by school_name and aggregate average reading_score
result = joined.groupby("school_name", as_index=False).agg({"reading_score": "mean"})

# Write output with exact target schema and column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_66/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
